extracted.intended_audience: Students and early career health librarians in academia, hospitals, and health research agencies who are interested in working on systematic review teams.
extracted.subtask_description: A professional development webinar syllabus focused on the librarian's role in planning, executing, and peer-reviewing systematic review search strategies and evidence gathering for health sciences systematic reviews. Emphasizes practical skills (database selection, search peer review) and awareness of standards and certification options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define a systematic review and explain how it differs from other review types
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a systematic review and explain how it differs from other review types
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You’ll learn the purpose and process of conducting systematic reviews, with an emphasis on the librarian’s role in supporting reviews, start to finish. You’ll understand why systematic reviews are more rigorous than other types of reviews and why this increased rigour puts them at the top of evidence pyramids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify key characteristics of and standards for high-quality reviews and review search strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify key characteristics of and standards for high-quality reviews and review search strategies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning outcome calls for recognising standards and characteristics that define high-quality reviews and their search strategies (implying comprehensiveness, reproducibility, rigor). The course emphasizes the librarian’s contribution to meeting these standards during evidence gathering and search construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe the librarian’s role a systematic review and identify key tools and approaches used at each stage of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the librarian’s role a systematic review and identify key tools and approaches used at each stage of the review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states that systematic review librarians are typically accountable for the evidence gathering stage of a review. Guidance/examples include supporting reviews 'start to finish' and identifying tools/approaches used at each stage (e.g., databases, search tools, peer review of searches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply transferable information skills to select databases and other search tools and sources for systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply transferable information skills to select databases and other search tools and sources for systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants will practice selecting appropriate databases and search tools as part of hands-on exercises; this criterion emphasises the ability to map a review question to suitable sources and justify database/tool choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice key skills by selecting databases and peer reviewing a systematic review search strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice key skills in this area by selecting databases and peer reviewing a systematic review search strategy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit course activity: hands-on exercises where learners select databases and peer-review a search strategy. Implies skills in constructing, evaluating, and improving search strategies for completeness and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin to develop fundamental skills in conducting reviews through hands-on exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: You’ll begin to develop fundamental skills in conducting reviews through hands-on exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on applied learning—building baseline competencies for contributing to systematic reviews (e.g., evidence gathering, search design, peer review of searches) rather than mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify options for professional reviewer certification open to librarians from leading local and international systematic review collaboratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify options for professional reviewer certification open to librarians from leading local and international systematic review collaboratives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course will point learners to certification opportunities (example: the presenter completed Comprehensive Systematic Review Training Certification from the Joanna Briggs Institute). This criterion concerns awareness of credentialing paths and professional development resources.
